title: [P0] Make the Firebase WAL durable, ordered, and safe during concurrent enqueue
body:
## Verified failure
At audited commit 356971d, `MachineA_BatteryCart/wal.py` snapshots the queue, uploads outside its lock, then replaces the entire queue with `remaining`. Enqueues during upload disappear. A failed older write does not stop later writes; on retry the older write overwrites the newer state. `_save_queue()` truncates the only JSON file in place and swallows disk errors. `_load_queue()` silently resets corrupt data to an empty queue.

## Reproduction
Offline checks `test_wal_retains_enqueue_during_flush`, `test_wal_failed_write_preserves_order`, `test_wal_reports_disk_failure`, and `test_wal_corrupt_file_requires_recovery` in the local audit harness fail. A flush-time enqueue leaves queue size 0 instead of 1. A failed charging-start followed by successful removal eventually leaves remote `IsCharging=True`.

## Suggested change
Use a transactional SQLite outbox or equivalent atomic, fsync-backed journal. Assign stable event IDs and acknowledge only successfully committed IDs; preserve ordering within a battery/session. Surface disk-full/corruption failures and preserve recovery evidence. Separate coalescible heartbeat/recommendation updates from immutable history; bound storage without discarding battery events.

## Acceptance
Test simultaneous producer/consumer activity, failed older writes, duplicate delivery, crash before/after upload acknowledgment, truncated storage, disk full, and an extended outage. Every durable battery event survives restart and reaches Firebase exactly once logically, in session order. This revalidates the resilience claimed by closed issue #2.

title: [P0] Read RFID independently of stdin so the installed cart service can run
body:
## Verified failure
`MachineA_BatteryCart/install.sh` creates a systemd service with no input device or StandardInput configuration. `input_listener.py:565-578` reads RFID using `input()` in the main thread. With service stdin closed, `EOFError` exits the process and all daemon workers; Restart=always creates a restart loop. A keyboard wedge also delivers scans to the focused GUI, not automatically to a service's stdin.

## Reproduction
`test_rfid_input_with_service_stdin_closed` fails against the extracted real listener. A foreground terminal test is insufficient evidence for the installed service.

## Suggested change
Read the dedicated RFID HID/evdev device or a configured serial reader; identify it persistently and grant only required device access to the service user. Handle unplug/replug, EOF, invalid scans and duplicate scans explicitly. Keep manual stdin mode as a deliberate development option.

## Acceptance
Install on a clean Pi, reboot without an interactive terminal, scan tags while Chromium has focus, unplug/replug RFID, and confirm one durable event per scan with no restart loop.

title: [P0] Make charge sessions and pull finalization local-first and atomic
body:
## Source-confirmed failure
`input_listener.py:391-415` reads charging history from Firebase before queuing a placement. Removal waits only 3 seconds, but WAL flushes every 30 seconds. `finalize_charging_removal` reads the remote slot/history, edits the last remote record, and directly writes IsCharging=False outside the WAL. A pull before its placement upload sees no record; an outage can kill the serial handler or abandon finalization permanently. Whole-array history replacement can lose intervening changes.

The flicker-resume branch falls through into common new-record creation: it uses an earlier `getCurrentChargingRecords` value (or an uninitialized value) and resets ChargingStartTime despite claiming to resume. Removal timers are in memory only, and key membership is checked without comparing the scheduled removal timestamp, so an earlier timer can consume a newer removal for the same slot/tag. The supplied slot_num is not used to identify the remote session being closed.

## Suggested change
Persist an authoritative local session with immutable session/event IDs before cloud access. Debounce with cancellation tied to that exact session and removal generation. Close that session, record its cycle/pull request, and update the live cache in one replayable atomic multipath operation. Derive counts from history; do not overwrite an entire remote array or depend on upload having happened first.

## Acceptance
Place and pull within 30 seconds, do both offline, restart during grace, flicker repeatedly with/without repeated RFID, move a battery to another slot, and return it just after grace. Verify exact start/end times, one completed cycle/pull request, no overwritten history, and convergence after reconnect.

title: [P1] Recover serial workers and implement acknowledged, validated LED commands
body:
## Verified/source-confirmed failure
`handle_serial()` retries opening initially but breaks out of its read loop and returns after an unplug; it never closes/removes the stale serial object or reopens. Heartbeat continues to report connected based on dictionary membership. `test_serial_reader_reopens_after_unplug` reproduces this.

LED `wait_for_ack()` clears the event after sending, losing an immediate ACK. Bare ACK has no command identity, so delayed ACKs can acknowledge a different command. Commands may remain suppressed by last_sent_command after a board reset. PONG is ignored. Firmware declares SERIAL_TIMEOUT but never checks it, leaving a stale green recommendation after communications stop. Slot messages accept arbitrary integers/states without validating their board's range.

## Suggested change
Use a supervised reopen loop with read/write timeouts, port cleanup, health from recent valid responses and worker liveness, per-command IDs, clearing ACK state before sending, reset-aware command-cache invalidation, and firmware timeout fallback. Strictly validate complete commands and slot messages before acknowledging or changing state.

## Acceptance
Unplug either Arduino, reset board 1, send immediate/late/duplicate ACKs and malformed messages, stall a port, and stop Pi heartbeats. Recover without service restart; report disconnected promptly; stale pick LEDs must clear/fallback.

title: [P1] Replace the startup timing window with an explicit slot snapshot handshake
body:
## Source-confirmed mismatch
The cart sets startup_block=True and waits four seconds for PRESENT messages (`input_listener.py:812-849`). Both sketches initialize lastState from analogRead in setup and only emit SLOT messages when state changes. They do not publish initially occupied slots or implement a snapshot request. An already occupied cart therefore appears empty at Pi startup. A delayed board can also miss the fixed startup window. Removing one untagged startup slot may clear the global block before other boards have reported.

## Suggested change
Introduce board identity/protocol version plus a complete initial snapshot and explicit resync request. Mark each board/slot unknown until synchronization completes; reconcile persisted sessions with hardware without inventing RFID identity. Do not infer empty from silence.

## Acceptance
Boot with all slots empty, partially occupied, fully occupied, one Arduino delayed/missing, and batteries already in Firebase. Restart Pi only and reset either Arduino. Correctly show occupied/unknown slots and the deliberate operator recovery workflow without false available/ready indicators. This revalidates closed issue #3.

title: [P1] Make RFID-to-slot matching unambiguous and bound stale scan state
body:
## Source-confirmed gap
`input_listener.py` matches the first pending tag within a global three-second window, regardless of reader/slot identity. Matching deliberately releases the shared lock for a second and does not revalidate the slot/session afterward. Multiple inserts can bind the wrong batteries; stale pending_tags are never expired, and duplicate scans can assign one battery to multiple slots. Unmatched PRESENT is ignored rather than exposed as occupied-but-unidentified. Removal cleanup deletes expired recent_removals opportunistically from another PRESENT handler and can race finalization timers.

## Suggested change
Use bounded scan expiration/deduplication and an explicit slot session state machine. Enforce one active slot per battery and revalidate state after waits. Associate reader identity when hardware permits; otherwise require operator confirmation for ambiguous matches rather than choosing the first tag. Show unknown/ambiguous occupancy. Use monotonic timers for matching/debounce.

## Acceptance
Replay two simultaneous inserts, swapped scan order, scan after PRESENT, duplicate scans, scan without insertion, removal during the one-second wait, clock jumps, and long scan-only sessions. No wrong identity, unbounded list, or falsely available slot. Hardware cross-talk is separately tracked in #10 and must be bench-tested.

title: [P1] Validate scoring records and configuration; isolate malformed observations
body:
## Verified failure
`battery_scoring/models.py` accepts negative/nonfinite currentVoltage and retains optional inputs without numeric/range validation. Invalid timestamps become None; match_score then treats missing timestamp as fully fresh. `_parse_timestamp` only catches ValueError, so unexpected types can raise TypeError. `firebase_store.list_measurements/list_cba_tests` assume dictionary shapes and do not isolate parse failures per observation. One malformed record can prevent that battery from being scored. Config validation checks version only.

## Reproduction
The negative-voltage, NaN-voltage and missing-timestamp audit checks fail. Undated 12.9 V produces 100 Match Score with .45 confidence.

## Suggested change
Validate finite numeric types, configurable plausible ranges and explicit units; reject or quarantine invalid shape/date/future timestamps with an auditable reason. Preserve the original raw record. Isolate invalid observations so valid history remains usable. Validate nonnegative weights, nonzero totals, ordered ranges, and freshness/trend limits. Define behavior for corrections/deletions without retaining a misleading cache.

## Acceptance
Test null, absent fields, zero where meaningful, strings, booleans, NaN/Infinity, wrong units, invalid and future timestamps, non-dict records and invalid configurations. Every published score/confidence is finite and bounded; unknown freshness is not fresh. Firebase rules should enforce the writer contract too.

title: [P1] Fix overlapping Health Score trend windows and conservative baseline selection
body:
## Verified failure
Default baseline_sample_size=5 and recent_sample_size=5 with min_points_for_trend=3 causes both windows to cover exactly the same data for 3-5 observations. `_trend_change_pct([8,10,14,20,25],5,5,3)` returns 0 despite substantial resistance growth; the corresponding component reports excellent condition. Overlapping windows continue to dilute the trend at 6-9 observations.

CBA always takes the first test as baseline, with no reliability selection or suspicious-reading safeguards. A single very low first capacity becomes its own 100% SOH, and old CBA contributes unchanged weight/confidence. Age/cycles alone can yield Health=100 at .2 confidence; this needs deliberate UX treatment.

## Suggested change
Require distinct baseline/recent windows and enough independent samples, or mark trend unknown. Establish an auditable reliable battery-specific baseline, quarantine/flag suspect changes, and configure freshness/confidence for sparse CBA history. Surface actual baseline, capacity SOH, dates and confidence; do not infer exact remaining life.

## Acceptance
Test 0-10 samples, rising/falling/flat sequences, outliers and corrected baseline readings, one CBA, old CBA and multiple seasons. Insufficient evidence must not claim a stable trend; meaningful degradation must move Health Score down.

title: [P1] Make the scoring service converge after stream failures, edits, and time decay
body:
## Verified/source-confirmed gap
`engine.py` ignores root '/' events because `_battery_id_from_event_path('/')` returns None. That excludes initial/reconnect full snapshots and root multipath patches; startup recompute before listeners attach also has a race window. Callback exceptions are unhandled by application code, listeners are not supervised, and the main process can stay alive without useful score updates. No periodic reconciliation occurs.

Only PullMeasurements and CBATests changes are observed: enrollment/purchase-date edits and Cycles-only changes do not recompute health/counts. Freshness and age change over time but cached scores remain unchanged until a new event/restart. Missing measurements cause an early return leaving a prior cache intact. Snapshot push and cache update are separate writes; concurrent callbacks can race and older results can overwrite newer ones. inputRefs contains only latest measurement/CBA, although Health used many measurements, counts, and battery metadata.

## Suggested change
Use per-battery serialized dirty work with retries/backoff, handle root payloads, supervise streams and reconcile periodically. Observe all relevant inputs and expire readiness by time. Atomically publish a snapshot/cache with source revision and full auditable input/baseline/config references. Handle correction/deletion and preserve latest available optional values with their own timestamps rather than erasing history's latest reading on a voltage-only pull.

## Acceptance
Inject root patches, missed/reconnect events, transient read/write failures, malformed records, two concurrent updates, metadata/cycle edits, deletions, and 72 hours without new input. Cache converges automatically and never regresses or silently stays fresh.

title: [P1] Make next-up recommendations safe for stale data, retirement, and all configured slots
body:
## Source-confirmed gap
`led_manager_loop` uses Firebase charging state rather than current local occupancy and only evaluates range(7), while board 2 emits slots 6-11. Sketch 1 has seven LED segments. The intended seven-slot versus twelve-slot physical layout needs an explicit shared configuration; slots 7-11 are currently omitted from recommendation/LED logic.

If Batteries lookup fails, the code silently substitutes {}, disabling retirement exclusion and reverting to charge-duration picks. Settings/minTime read failure becomes 0, making every charging battery eligible. Any cached Match Score outranks an unscored battery regardless of score age/confidence, invalid type, status or actual presence. Repeated next-up writes and heartbeats inflate the WAL while offline.

## Suggested change
Cache last-known validated settings/metadata locally, honor retirement/practice eligibility through outages, use hardware occupancy and acknowledged session state, and gate ranking on valid recent scores/confidence. Show unknown/unverified status instead of promoting batteries after failed reads. Define elapsed-time readiness as an operational heuristic; no charger voltage sensor proves charge completion. Centralize the intended slot/segment layout and coalesce unchanged recommendation updates.

## Acceptance
Test occupied-but-unidentified slots, retired/practice batteries, missing/invalid/stale scores, Firebase failure, invalid/missing minTime, every installed slot, and hours offline. No removed/retired/unknown battery is offered as the next-match pick.

title: [P1] Make Drive ingestion resumable, paginated, and keyed by file revision
body:
## Verified/source-confirmed failure
`drive_sync.list_new_files` requests only files and never follows nextPageToken; a fake two-page listing returns one page. `main.py` skips downloads whenever the destination path exists, including interrupted partial downloads. Exclusions use names only, so different Drive files with the same name collide and modified files are not reingested. DSConverter/dsevents mark filenames processed before persistent copy/filter success. A failed copy can then leave the wrapper believing there is nothing to retry.

Drive names are joined directly into local paths: '../outside.dslog' escapes temp and absolute paths also bypass it. The list query does not exclude trashed files, folder resolution chooses the first duplicate name, and folder names are interpolated without query escaping.

## Suggested change
Use a configured folder ID, complete pagination and extension/trashed filtering. Map Drive ID+revision/checksum to safe local names with containment/symlink checks. Download to temporary files and validate before atomic rename. Persist per-file processing stages, verify content hashes, and mark complete only after all required artifacts are durable. Retry incomplete stages and bound/rotate staging storage according to explicit retention policy.

## Acceptance
Test more than one page, duplicate names/folders, renamed/modified files, partial transfer, disk full, missing backup mount, failed conversion/copy/filter, crash at every stage, traversal/absolute names, and concurrent/manual runs. No permanent skip, wrong overwrite, escape, or success before durable output.

title: [P1] Preserve raw CSV data and make filtering idempotent and explicit
body:
## Verified failure
`filter_csv.process_csv(input_path, output_path)` ignores output_path and overwrites input_path with three columns. Running it twice turns total_current=3 into 0 because pdp_data_currents was removed on the first pass. `main.py` recopies all prior CSVs and refilters them on later runs, so a later ingestion can overwrite backups with degraded data. It copies before filtering, so persistent output is also one transformation behind the advertised cleaned result. Parse failures/missing currents silently become 0.

## Reproduction
`test_filter_honors_output_path` and `test_filter_repeat_preserves_current` fail on a one-row fixture. Voltage validation is tracked in existing #5.

## Suggested change
Retain immutable raw downloads/CSV and write a separate versioned derived CSV atomically to the requested output path. Filter only raw input or make repeated conversion demonstrably idempotent. Represent missing/invalid current as unknown with quality flags, not a real zero; preserve per-channel/status/brownout fields needed for future analysis. Publish and verify the intended derived artifact after transformation.

## Acceptance
Repeated runs and arrival of a second log never change previously correct raw/current data. Separate output mode leaves input untouched; interrupted writes preserve last good output; malformed and missing measurements are flagged.

title: [P1] Correct CTRE current bit extraction and reject truncated DS log records
body:
## Verified failure
`dslogtocsvlibrary/entry/pdp_ctre_data.py` shifts packed values without masking to ten bits or emulating fixed-width left-shift overflow. A synthetic record encoding 1 A on every channel decodes channel 1 as 1025 A, later channels as over 10^15 A. `test_ctre_currents_do_not_bleed_between_channels` reproduces this without external dependencies.

`DsLogStream.conditional_read` returns None for a short read, and iteration treats truncated records as clean EOF. DSConverter can therefore save a partial CSV and permanently exclude the source. CSV fieldnames are taken only from the first record; changes of controller/data shape can fail later rows, while processDSLogs catches failures and the converter still exits successfully.

## Suggested change
Mask the extracted ten-bit channel field and verify CTRE/REV formats against authoritative format definitions plus known-good DS logs. Distinguish clean record-boundary EOF from truncation and corrupt/unsupported metadata; propagate actionable per-file failures and never publish/exclude a partial parse as complete. Stream large records/output with a stable schema rather than retaining all records in memory.

## Acceptance
Known CTRE/REV/NONE fixtures with exact expected currents, all-zero/max/single-channel bit patterns, mixed metadata, truncated header and every record section, unknown type/version, and large files. No implausible current from bit leakage or silently successful partial conversion.

title: [P1] Make installation and updates verifiable, non-destructive, and restart-safe
body:
## Source-confirmed mismatch
MachineC installer declares offsite-check as Type=oneshot on a ten-minute timer, but check_and_run_main.py loops forever polling every ten seconds and ignores the child exit code. It does not behave as the documented periodic check and can repeatedly run failing pipelines. The generated update service does only git pull --ff-only: no dependency refresh, validation, restart or rollback, so live processes can retain old code and later imports can see new code. The README claim that local edits are always left unchanged is not enforced by an explicit clean/status guard.

Separately deploy.sh hard-codes /home/offsitecompute and uses git reset --hard origin/main, discarding tracked local work. Existing service files are skipped during install, so configuration fixes never reach older installs. Startup commands in MachineC swallow failures with || true before declaring success. MachineA uses system Python with --break-system-packages and leaves OS dependency installation commented out. Requirements are unpinned.

## Suggested change
Choose a bounded timer-driven one-shot or a supervised daemon and match the unit/readme. Fail visibly on failed processing/startup. Use a venv on both machines, tested locked dependencies and supported Python minimum. Explicitly refuse dirty/diverged checkouts; stage a verified release, migrate/update units deliberately, restart all relevant services and retain a rollback revision. Avoid automatic destructive reset or source updates beneath running services.

## Acceptance
Clean supported Linux installation, repeat installation over older units, missing dependencies/credentials/mounts, failed startup, clean/dirty/diverged updates, new dependency version, and rollback. Verify service active/healthy, timer behavior and running revision; never print success for a failed required service.

title: [P1] Verify the full FRC workflow and durable event contract across cart, kiosk, and Firebase
body:
## Readiness blocker, not a claim that the external UI is absent
The included FRC specification requires enrollment with name/brand/purchase date, every completed pull creating a cycle and mandatory-voltage popup, optional Beak values, separate CBA workflow, lifetime/season history, trends, confidence and fleet ranking. Shared/battery_schema.md assigns enrollment/Cycles/PullMeasurements/CBA writes to a separate BatteryTrackingWebsite repository, which is not part of this checkout. This repository contains no browser client, Firebase rules/index deployment, or end-to-end acceptance evidence. MachineA writes BatteryList/NameRequests; the scorer reads different Batteries/Cycles/PullMeasurements/CBATests nodes. These components cannot be declared integrated based on scoring code alone.

A kiosk watching only live IsCharging changes can miss offline/multi-pull transitions while closed/disconnected. Cycle IDs based on ChargingEndTime have only second-level timestamps and are not a persisted event delivery/acknowledgment protocol. Naming existence is checked against BatteryNames, not the complete enrollment record. The scorer counts every Cycles node, not specifically completed cycles, and does not populate seasonCycleCount.

## Suggested change
Link/pin the matching website release and check its AGENTS/workflow separately. Publish a durable PullRequests/event history with unique session IDs from the cart and let clients process/acknowledge pending requests idempotently. Ensure required fields are validated at the trusted write boundary and rules forbid unauthorized/history-destructive writes; deploy required query indexes. Derive lifetime/season counts from completed canonical cycles and audit corrections. Specify UTC timestamps and DST/clock-skew handling across Pi/VM/browser.

## Acceptance
Unknown scan requires all enrollment fields; each pull yields one cycle and one recoverable voltage request, including kiosk closed, multiple tabs, offline/reconnect and restart. Voltage-only submit works and omitted optional fields remain null. Separate CBA retains all seasons; corrections are auditable; scores/ranks/trends update; retired/practice filtering and confidence are visible. Preserve history across season/software/config changes. Confirm deployed Firebase permissions/indexes using an emulator then authorized live checks.
